title: Quickstart: reduce activation friction (env vars clarity, copy/paste curl, better startup errors)
author: Jada Williams
release_notes: Improves starter template onboarding: clearer required env vars, adds copy-paste curl verification step, and surfaces actionable error messages when misconfigured.
body:
Context: This PR is part of the lifecycle growth experiments sprint to reduce time-to-first-success for self-serve developers. We’ve seen a common failure mode where users clone the starter template, miss a required env var (or use the wrong key), and then hit a generic 401/400 that doesn’t explain what to do next. This PR makes the very first run path more deterministic and gives users a single copy/paste request (curl) to confirm the API key + project routing before they wire up the app.

What changed (high level): 1) Clarify required env vars and provide a safe .env.example 2) Add a copy/paste curl “sanity check” step in README that matches the Hosted API and console onboarding flow 3) Improve startup/runtime error messages for missing/invalid configuration (API key missing, wrong base URL, non-2xx response) with targeted next steps and links.

Details: - Added .env.example with explicit required variables and inline comments: REDWOOD_API_KEY (required), REDWOOD_BASE_URL (optional; defaults to https://api.redwoodinference.com), REDWOOD_MODEL (optional default). - README now includes a “Verify your key in 30 seconds” section with a curl request that users can run before starting the app. The curl example uses streaming off by default to simplify debugging, with an optional streaming variant below it. - Updated the Node starter template boot path to validate configuration early and fail fast with actionable errors (instead of crashing downstream or returning a generic fetch error). - Improved HTTP error mapping so the first failure message points to the likely fix: 401/403 -> check API key + permissions; 404 -> likely wrong base URL / route path; 429 -> rate limiting / free credits exhausted; >=500 -> retry + status page.

Illustrative snippets (not full diff): - README curl (non-streaming): curl -sS "$REDWOOD_BASE_URL/v1/chat/completions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"$REDWOOD_MODEL","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello from quickstart"}]}' - Env validation message: "Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY. Create an API key in Console → Settings → API Keys, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env. See: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart#api-key" - HTTP error message example: "Request failed (401 Unauthorized). Your API key is missing/invalid OR does not have access to this project. Double-check REDWOOD_API_KEY and that you’re using the right workspace/project.".

Why this approach: - The curl sanity check mirrors the activation definition we’ve been discussing (first successful production-like inference call). It gives a deterministic success path without requiring the full app to be correct. - Early validation avoids a confusing cascade of errors and reduces support load from “it doesn’t work” tickets. - Keeping base URL optional reduces the chance users copy an internal/staging endpoint from somewhere and then get a 404.

Testing: - Manual: fresh clone, node version matrix (18, 20), confirmed the quickstart runs with only REDWOOD_API_KEY set; confirmed errors for missing key and bad base URL. - Added lightweight unit tests for env validation + HTTP error mapping.

Rollout/notes: - This is a quickstarts-only change; no production impact. - Intended to be referenced by onboarding email CTAs and the console checklist “Make your first request” step.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add a small troubleshooting page section for “401 vs 403 vs 404” (Docs PR is tracked separately). - Consider adding an optional command: npm run verify-key that runs the curl check via node to avoid shell escaping issues on Windows.

Screenshots: - Included updated README sections in the PR files (no UI screenshots).

Link: Linear PM-413 (onboarding sequence requirements) + PM-412 (activation milestone definition).
commits: quickstart: add .env.example and tighten setup docs
starter(node): validate env and surface actionable errors
readme: add copy/paste curl verification step
tests: cover config validation + http error mapping
conversation:
Ben Carter (review): Love the curl sanity check. Can we make sure it matches the exact path + headers used in the onboarding emails (and UTMs won’t break anything)? Also, include a note for users who don’t have a model name yet.

Jada Williams (author): Updated the curl to /v1/chat/completions and kept headers minimal (Authorization + Content-Type). Added a default model in the README example and a note that any model from the catalog works; users can swap it after first success.

Marissa Cole (review): Error messages look good, but please avoid pointing to a console path that might change. Prefer a docs anchor if possible.

Jada Williams (author): Swapped Console deep links to docs anchors where we have stable URLs, and kept the console reference generic ("Console → API Keys").

Leila Farouk (review): Can we add a regression test for the case where REDWOOD_BASE_URL has a trailing slash and the constructed URL becomes double-slashed?

Jada Williams (author): Good catch. Normalized base URL in config and added a test.

Soojin Lee (review): Minor copy: avoid absolute claims like “30 seconds” in case of network issues. Maybe “under a minute”.

Jada Williams (author): Updated phrasing to “under a minute” and added a note about proxies/firewalls.

Ben Carter (follow-up): Any chance we can include a streaming curl variant too? Some devs specifically want streaming.

Jada Williams (author): Added a streaming variant below the basic one with a short warning about buffering in some terminals.

Status: Approved by Ben Carter, Marissa Cole, Leila Farouk. Merged (squash) after CI green.
